title: Money, quotes, follow-ups
lead: Is lesson ke baad tum quote, invoice, advance aur payment follow-up English me politely handle kar paoge — bina awkward silence ke.
description: Week 10 English lesson: share a quote, send an invoice, ask for an advance, and follow up on payment politely.

patterns.say: The cost is fifteen thousand rupees.
patterns.positive: The cost is fifteen thousand rupees.
patterns.question: What is the total cost?
examples: The cost is twenty thousand rupees plus GST.
Kharche bees hazaar rupaye plus GST hain.
The monthly cost is five thousand rupees.
Monthly kharche paanch hazaar rupaye hain.
patterns.grammar: cost is + amount. cost = total; price = ek item ka daam. hundred/thousand/lakh singular rehte hain.
patterns.mistake: “The cost is fifteen thousands” → “The cost is fifteen thousand.” Thousand singular.

patterns.note: Amount, date ya scope confirm karne ke liye.
patterns.say: Could you confirm the advance amount?
patterns.positive: Could you confirm the advance amount?
patterns.negative: I can't confirm the discount yet.
patterns.question: Could you confirm the payment date?
examples: Could you confirm the final amount?
Kya aap final amount confirm kar sakte hain?
Could you confirm the invoice details?
Kya aap invoice details confirm kar sakte hain?
patterns.grammar: Could you confirm + noun/clause. Polite confirmation. confirm + thing, not person.
patterns.mistake: “Could you confirm me the amount?” → “Could you confirm the amount?” confirm + thing.

patterns.note: Direct but polite — please add karo.
patterns.say: We need the payment before delivery.
patterns.positive: We need the payment before delivery.
patterns.negative: We don't need the full amount now.
patterns.question: When can we expect the payment?
examples: We need the advance to start the work.
Kaam shuru karne ke liye advance chahiye.
We need the balance before the final handover.
Final handover se pehle balance chahiye.
patterns.grammar: need + noun. before + noun/-ing. Please se tone soft karo.
patterns.mistake: “We need to payment” → “We need the payment.” Noun ke pehle to nahi.

patterns.negative: I haven't sent the invoice yet.
patterns.question: Did you send the invoice?
examples: I'll send the invoice on email.
Main email par invoice bhej doonga.
I've sent the invoice on WhatsApp.
Maine WhatsApp par invoice bhej diya hai.
patterns.grammar: invoice = bill. send the invoice. by email / on WhatsApp.
patterns.mistake: “I'll send you invoice” → “I'll send you the invoice.” Article the chahiye.

patterns.say: When can we expect the payment?
patterns.positive: When can we expect the payment?
patterns.negative: I'm not sure when we can expect it.
patterns.question: When can we expect the next update?
examples: When can we expect the advance?
Advance kab tak expect kar sakte hain?
When can we expect the purchase order?
Purchase order kab tak milega?
patterns.grammar: When can + subject + base verb. expect + noun. Polite follow-up.
patterns.mistake: “When we can expect payment?” → “When can we expect the payment?” Can subject se pehle.

patterns.note: Soft follow-up — pressure kam, reminder clear.
patterns.say: Is there any update on the payment?
patterns.positive: Is there any update on the payment?
patterns.question: Is there any update on the invoice?
examples: Is there any update on the advance?
Advance par koi update hai?
Is there any update on the approval?
Approval par koi update hai?
patterns.grammar: Is there any update on + noun? Follow-up ka polite tarika.
patterns.mistake: “Any update on payment?” is okay informally, but “Is there any update on the payment?” polite hota hai.

dialogue.context: Payment follow-up call. Riya = client. Invoice, total, advance aur discount — politely cover karo.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: Hi, we haven't received the invoice yet.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Sorry about that. I'll send the invoice today.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: The cost is fifteen thousand rupees, plus GST. We need the advance before we start.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: We can offer a five percent discount on the total. Could you confirm the advance by Friday?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Great. Is there any update on the purchase order?

dialogue.closing: Money conversation me teen cheezein clear: amount, date, next step. Guess mat karo, confirm karo.

I'll send the quote by Monday.

selfCheck: “Could you confirm ___?” se ek cheez confirm ki.
Advance ya payment ki zaroorat clear batayi.

pronunciation.title: Numbers
pronunciation.body: fifteen /fɪfˈtiːn/ vs fifty /ˈfɪfti/. Stress end me fifteen, start me fifty.

pronunciation.title: Lakh/crore vs million
pronunciation.body: 1 lakh = 100,000; 1 crore = 10 million. Client Indian ho to lakh/crore, international ho to million bolo.

pronunciation.title: Linking
pronunciation.body: Could you → /wʊdʒə/. “Could you confirm” ko “could-ja confirm” jaisa jodo.

followUps: Payment follow-up me kitna direct hona chahiye?
Lakh/crore ko international client ko kaise bataun?
Advance na mile to kaam kaise handle karun?
Discount dene ka best time kya hai?
mission: Record a payment follow-up message: amount, invoice, advance date, and polite reminder.
